newsitem.title: USA: Food Lion, ABC jurors asked to talk ethics.
newsitem.headline: Food Lion, ABC jurors asked to talk ethics.

text.p: The ABC television network, ordered to pay Food Lion Inc., $5.5 million in punitive damages stemming from an undercover report on the supermarket chain, said Friday it invited jurors from the case to participate in a program about journalism ethics.
Earlier in January, ABC lost a civil law suit by the Salisbury, N.C.-based supermarket chain, which sued ABC over a 1992 PrimeTime Live report.

Food Lion, based in Salisbury, N.C., sued ABC over a 1992 "PrimeTime Live" report that charged Food Lion sold spoiled meat and other outdated merchandise and did not use sanitary food handling practices.
During the civil trial, the jury found ABC had committed fraud, trespass and breach of loyalty, and earlier this month recommended ABC pay punitive damages of $5.5 million to Food Lion.
During the trial, the store addressed ABC's newsgathering procedures rather than the content of the program.
Now ABC, a New York-based unit of Walt Disney Co., wants the jurors for a Feb. 12, broadcast of PrimeTime Live that will focus on investigative journalism.
"The verdict in this case has sparked a public debate about the role of the media, and the relationship of the press to the public," the network said in a statement.
As part of the PrimeTime Live broadcast on Feb. 12, the report from the Nov. 5, 1992 broadcast will be shown, as well as past PrimeTime Live investigative reports.
The judge would not allow replaying the piece during the trial. Food Lion is a unit of Belgian retailer Ets Delhaize Freres et Cie "LE LION' SA.
